findings.statement: Top of the convergence ranking, strongly tumour-up and replicated in TCGA. Membrane protein (cell membrane, microvillus membrane), so it is suitable for antibodies and as a circulating or imaging marker. Open Targets tractability lists antibody evidence. Known drugs: girentuximab (PHASE_3), iodine-124 labelled girentuximab (PHASE_2), sulthiame (PHASE_4), ethoxzolamide (WITHDRAWAL). DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency (no ccRCC lines dependent, not common essential), so the case rests on a surface-antigen strategy (antibody, radioligand, imaging) and not on inhibiting its function. The most ccRCC-selective PRISM compound, para-toluenesulfonamide, hits several targets and is not significant after correction, so it says little about CA9.

High in the convergence ranking. Tumour-up, with signal robust to tumour purity, and replicated in TCGA. Plasma membrane ligand of CD27, with Open Targets tractability labels AB Advanced Clinical and OC Advanced Clinical. Drugs: cusatuzumab (PHASE_2), vorsetuzumab and vorsetuzumab mafodotin (PHASE_1), MDX-1411 (PHASE_1). Pathway: TNFs bind their physiological receptors. DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency and no common essentiality, so this is an antigen-targeting case (ADC, CAR-T, antibody) and not a functional-dependency case.

Mid-table in the top-40 convergence ranking. Tumour-up and purity-robust. Apical cell membrane and secreted ectoenzyme that hydrolyses extracellular nucleotides and the cyclic dinucleotide cGAMP. Clinical drug: AGS-16C3F (PHASE_2), an antibody-drug conjugate. This is a tractable antigen with prior clinical testing in renal cancer. DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency, so the case rests on an ADC strategy.

Established ccRCC target (HIF-2 alpha). Lower in the top-40 convergence ranking, but it is the only top-40 gene with a ccRCC-selective DepMap dependency: ccRCC lines are more dependent than other lines, and about a fifth of ccRCC lines are dependent, although the Welch q-value is borderline. Open Targets lists belzutifan (APPROVAL). The PRISM hit PT-2385 (PHASE_1, a single-target HIF inhibitor) is directionally selective but not significant, and 2D culture under-represents HIF-2 biology. Mutation is rare, so the dependency comes from the VHL-HIF axis and not from EPAS1 mutation.

Top Open Targets association with ccRCC (first in the disease top-targets list) and a clear somatic driver: it is mutated in about half of tumours, with a highly significant excess over background. It is a tumour suppressor, not a direct drug target. It matters as the upstream mechanism of HIF-2 alpha stabilisation, which makes belzutifan therapy rational. DepMap selectivity is strongly negative, consistent with loss of VHL being tolerated in ccRCC lines. No drugs are annotated.

High in the convergence ranking. It has genetic association in Open Targets, with a moderate overall score, and is tumour-up and purity-robust with TCGA replication. Open Targets lists tractability but no drugs. DepMap shows no dependency. It is tractable but untested in ccRCC, and its lipid-uptake role is a plausible mechanism.

High in the convergence ranking. Tumour-up, purity-robust and replicated. High expression is associated with worse prognosis (Cox hazard ratio above one, significant after correction) and with higher grade. Predicted tractable (small molecule), no clinical drug. DepMap shows no dependency in ccRCC (mean effect positive), so it is better supported as a prognostic biomarker than as a target. The Open Targets association is weak.

In the upper part of the convergence ranking. Tumour-up and purity-robust glycolytic lactate transporter (MCT4), predicted tractable, with no clinical drug annotated. DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency and no selectivity, so druggability without dependency is a weaker target case.

Near the top of the convergence ranking. Strongly down in tumour, replicated in TCGA, with lower expression linked to worse survival (protective Cox hazard ratio below one). It is a proximal-tubule metabolic marker with no drugs and weak Open Targets association. It is a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker candidate, not a target.

Near the top of the convergence ranking. Down in tumour, with loss associated with worse survival. Organic anion transporter, with probenecid (PHASE_4) and pratosartan (PHASE_3) annotated as transporter-directed drugs. These are not antitumour therapies. This is a loss-of-expression biomarker of proximal-tubule identity, not a target.

High in the convergence ranking. Down in tumour and replicated. It has an Open Targets genetic-association component. No drugs. Because it is a secreted immunoglobulin transporter, it could be measured in body fluids. This is association-only and has no dependency evidence.

In the top-40 convergence ranking. Tumour-up lipid droplet protein, purity-robust and replicated in TCGA, with a favourable association with survival. No tractability annotated and no drugs. It is a candidate tissue biomarker of the lipid-rich clear cell phenotype.

caveats: Numeric values are described in words because the cited records were not individually annotated; exact values are in the convergence ranking output.
Most top-ranked genes show no ccRCC-selective DepMap dependency, so antigen-directed strategies (CA9, CD70, ENPP3) rest on surface expression and not on functional essentiality.
Dependency, mutation and PRISM were checked only for a subset of genes (CA9, CD70, EPAS1, ENPP3, SLC16A3, NNMT, VHL).
The cell lines are grown in 2D and under-represent HIF-2 biology, so the weak PRISM signal for EPAS1 does not argue against belzutifan.
Several drugs listed for transporter genes (probenecid, diuretics, SGLT2 inhibitors) are annotation-only and not antitumour.
